correctness.rationale: Every maximal matching of a one-leaf corona corresponds uniquely to a core matching extended by pendants at its unsaturated vertices. An observation collision has an alternating symmetric difference consisting only of omitted core edges, with each alternating path having two vertices with omitted pendant edges. Such a collision exists exactly when the omitted-core graph contains an even cycle or has a component containing two omitted-pendant vertices. Optimization gives m minus the maximum cycle rank of even-cycle-free spanning subgraphs, and classifies all minimum observations. The no-even-cycle equivalence to odd cacti, bipartite sharpness, Fibonacci path enumerator, cycle parity and complete-graph formula follow from explicit arguments. Standalone verification exhaustively checks all labeled graphs of order at most four (75 graphs total) and all observation subsets, paths and cycles to order seven, and six further test families. No finite search is used to prove the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The accessible original corona-product paper proves bounds, specifically the bound m for one-leaf coronas, but not the new exact odd-cactus formula, obstruction characterization, all-minimizer classification, all-graph bipartite equality criterion, or Fibonacci minimizer count. The accessible graph-operations work is neither equivalent nor stronger. Independent original-text and record searches produced no result covering these statements. This is a bounded literature assessment rather than proof of uniqueness; inaccessible foundational 2018 full text remains a concrete residual risk.
residual_risks: The complete text of the 2018 foundational article was not accessible; the abstract and later citations do not conclusively exclude every theorem in its appendices.
Other indexed or unpublished work using a nonstandard forcing/identifying terminology could have equivalent coverage.
This is a self-review, not independent audit or external certification.

value.rationale: The motivating 2021 corona-product article left the precise scope of its one-leaf upper bound open beyond a small sharpness example. The theorem gives a simultaneous, exact characterization of all distinguishing sets for every finite simple base graph, a transparent structural optimization using odd cactus cycle rank, and the exact bipartite/nonbipartite transition. A nontrivial enumeration of all minimizers on whiskered paths gives the Fibonacci sequence at even indices. These are motivated classifications and infinite-family consequences, not arbitrary finite computations or merely an algebraic restatement of the known upper bound.
